'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#DECDE6|30–40%}} {{legend0|#D2B1D9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#AE8BB1|50–60%}} {{legend0|#808080|'''No data'''}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Tom Ridge]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Tom Ridge]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsPA}} The '''1998 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election''' was held on November 3, 1998 to elect the [[Governor of Pennsylvania|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Pennsylvania|lieutenant governor of Pennsylvania]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Tom Ridge]] was re-elected to a second term in office over [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state representative [[Ivan Itkin]] and anti-abortion activist Peg Luksik. As of 2026, this was the last gubernatorial election in which [[Delaware County, Pennsylvania|Delaware]], [[Lackawanna County, Pennsylvania|Lackawanna]] or [[Montgomery County, Pennsylvania|Montgomery]] counties voted for the Republican candidate and the last time a Republican was re-elected as governor of Pennsylvania. It was also the first time since [[1930 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election|1930]] that [[Greene County, Pennsylvania|Greene]], [[Fayette County, Pennsylvania|Fayette]], or [[Washington County, Pennsylvania|Washington]] counties voted Republican. == Republican primary == Incumbent Governor Ridge ran unopposed for the Republican nomination, and was endorsed by multiple newspapers across the state, including the ''York Daily Record''."[https://www.newspapers.com/image/555138888/?terms=%22Tom%20Ridge%22&match=1 Today is the day to have your say]." Itkin, who had little name recognition statewide, was considered to be a sacrificial lamb. Peg Luksik, who was well known as an outspoken opponent of abortion, ran as a strong third party contender for the second consecutive election cycle; she emphasized the pro-choice stances of both candidates and drew votes in the state's rural, conservative center. However, Ridge's victory was never in doubt, as he ran on a generally positive record from his prior term and a combination of traditional Republican strategies (such as his "tough on crime" image) combined with his ability to somewhat undercut Democratic support (such as through his labor ties).{{cite book|last=Kennedy|first=John J.|title=Pennsylvania Elections: Statewide Contests From 1950-2004|year=2006|publisher=University Press of America|isbn=9780761832799|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1J_9q-lIWRkC&q=1998+ridge+itkin}} ===Polling=== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign="bottom" !
